title: q.calendar Roadmap

---
title: q.calendar Roadmap
---

Only open work is listed here. The existing `schedule` and
`non_trading_days_after` functions are the foundation for the work below.

## Design rules

- Every public operation requires an explicit ISO 10383 exchange identifier.
- Session labels are timezone-naive normalized dates; market timestamps are
	timezone-aware and expressed in either UTC or the exchange's IANA timezone.
- APIs must define their behavior for timestamps before the open, after the
	close, during holidays, and at daylight-saving transitions.
- Early closes are ordinary trading sessions with a shorter interval, not
	holidays or incomplete observations.
- `q.calendar` owns exchange-time semantics. It may construct labels and time
	grids, but OHLCV aggregation and market-data mutation belong to `q.data`.

## Session navigation and classification

- [ ] Add scalar and vectorized session predicates:

	```python
	q.calendar.is_session("2024-03-28", exchange="XSTO")
	q.calendar.is_early_close("2024-03-28", exchange="XSTO")
	```

	The vectorized form should preserve the input index, reject missing dates by
	default, and distinguish a closed date from an unknown/out-of-range calendar.

- [ ] Add `previous_session` and `next_session` with an explicit `include_self`
	option and positive integer offsets. The implementation must use exchange
	sessions rather than subtracting calendar days.

- [ ] Add `session_open`, `session_close`, and `session_bounds`. Returned
	timestamps must be timezone-aware in the exchange's local timezone by default,
	with `tz="UTC"` as an explicit alternative.

- [ ] Add session classification metadata to `schedule`, either through
	optional columns or a separate `session_flags` function:
	`is_early_close`, `is_late_open`, regular duration, actual duration, and the
	applicable local UTC offset.

## Timestamp-to-session alignment

- [ ] Add a vectorized `session_labels` operation:

	```python
	labels = q.calendar.session_labels(
			timestamps,
			exchange="XSTO",
			direction="none",
			include_close=False,
	)
	```

	It should assign each timestamp to the exchange session that contains it.
	`direction="none"` returns missing labels or raises for out-of-session values;
	`"previous"` and `"next"` explicitly opt into nearest-session alignment.

- [ ] Define interval boundaries once and test them consistently. The proposed
	default is `[open, close)`, with an opt-in policy for official closing prints
	timestamped exactly at the close.

- [ ] Support timestamps supplied in UTC, the exchange timezone, or another
	timezone. Reject timezone-naive intraday timestamps unless the caller passes
	an explicit `assume_timezone` value; never silently interpret them as local.

- [ ] Add `session_for_timestamp` as a scalar convenience wrapper over the same
	implementation. Scalar and vectorized results must not diverge.

- [ ] Cover ambiguous and nonexistent local times around daylight-saving
	changes. Resolution must be explicit and deterministic rather than delegated
	to pandas defaults that can vary by operation.

## Trading-time grids

- [ ] Add `trading_minutes` and a general `trading_ranges` API for one or many
	sessions. Inputs should support an exchange, frequency, start/end session,
	and interval-closure policy.

- [ ] Ensure generated grids respect holidays, half days, late opens, and any
	exchange breaks represented by the upstream calendar.

- [ ] Add a compact session-offset representation suitable for assigning large
	tick tables without materializing every minute when only labels are needed.

- [ ] Expose enough interval metadata for `q.data.resample_trades` to aggregate
	by exchange session without duplicating calendar logic. `q.calendar` should
	not itself choose OHLC, volume, quote, or empty-bar policies.

## Calendar distance

- [ ] Add trading-session distance and trading-minute distance between two
	timestamps for one exchange.

- [ ] Add multi-exchange overlap features: common sessions, union sessions,
	simultaneous open intervals, and distance to the next overlap. These are
	needed for cross-market features and FX/cash-conversion availability.

- [ ] Define signed distance, endpoint inclusion, and non-session alignment
	explicitly. Calendar-day, session, and trading-minute distances must remain
	separate concepts in names and return metadata.

## Performance and caching

- [ ] Cache immutable exchange-calendar lookups and bounded schedules without
	leaking mutable DataFrames between callers.

- [ ] Provide vectorized implementations for million-row timestamp indexes;
	avoid Python loops over observations.

- [ ] Benchmark session labeling and minute-grid generation across XNYS, XSTO,
	and an exchange with an intraday break.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests for normal sessions, XSTO half days, holidays, weekends,
	daylight-saving boundaries, exact opens/closes, and out-of-range dates.
- [ ] Property tests that every generated trading timestamp maps back to the
	session that generated it and no closed-date timestamp is emitted.
- [ ] Cross-check representative schedules against `exchange_calendars` while
	keeping QRT's public errors, timezone policy, and result schemas stable.
- [ ] Integration tests with the future `q.data` session-aware resampler and
	point-in-time universe snapshot builder.
